A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same Scaffold-SLAM paper. All 11 pages, including equations, figures, tables, and references, support comparison. Neither supplied PDF contains an appendix. The only visible difference is the first-page arXiv version/date stamp.

before.justification: v1 reports original tracking, rendering, runtime, and ablation results on Replica, TUM RGB-D, and EuRoC MAV in Section 4 and Tables 1–5.

after.justification: v2 retains the same original experimental results in Section 4 and Tables 1–5. Their retention from v1 does not alter their status as original empirical results.

M1.justification: Section 3 retains the identical localization pipeline, structured Gaussian representation, Appearance-from-Motion embedding, frequency regularization pyramid, and optimization objectives.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate Replica and TUM RGB-D with monocular and RGB-D cameras, and EuRoC MAV with stereo cameras. No datasets, tasks, or test scenarios change.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is identical in corresponding experiments in Tables 1–3, including MonoGS, Photo-SLAM, Photo-SLAM-30K, the additional RGB-D methods, and the tracking comparators.

E3.justification: Section 4.1 retains the same 30K-iteration default, ATE RMSE and rendering metrics, exclusion of training keyframes from rendering evaluation, and unmasked RGB-D evaluation procedure.

E4.justification: The component-removal and component-replacement ablations in Section 4.3 and Tables 4–5 are identical. The associated qualitative analyses and examples also remain unchanged.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests for its experiments. Statistical reporting practices are unchanged.

E6.justification: All numerical entries in Tables 1–5 and qualitative results match. For example, Table 1 reports Scaffold-SLAM RGB-D PSNR values of 39.14 on Replica and 25.95 on TUM RGB-D in both versions.

T1.justification: Equations 1–9 and their mathematical reasoning and assumptions are identical. No definitions, derivations, theorems, or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same two methodological contributions and claims of superior photorealistic mapping across three camera types with competitive tracking accuracy.

C2.justification: Both versions give the same interpretations of depth dependence, appearance modeling, frequency supervision, and rendering versus runtime tradeoffs. The future-work statement about improving real-time performance is unchanged.

D1.justification: Implementation disclosures remain identical, including LibTorch/C++/CUDA, ORB-SLAM3 localization, RTX 4090 and Threadripper hardware, and the promise of publicly available code. No technical or access information changes.

R1.justification: The related-work discussion, positioning relative to Photo-SLAM and other methods, and all 58 references are unchanged.

P1.justification: Only the first-page margin stamp changes from arXiv v1 dated 9 Jan 2025 to v2 dated 26 Feb 2025. The paper's prose, headings, author information, terminology, and section structure are identical.

P2.justification: Figures 1–6 and Tables 1–5 retain identical content, captions, formatting, and placement. Rendered pages match apart from the version/date text recorded under P1; the document layout is unchanged.

improvement.justification: The complete supplied PDFs contain identical scientific content, evidence, explanations, and presentation apart from the arXiv version/date stamp. This administrative update neither resolves a deficiency nor harms the paper's overall quality.
